- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates sharp drops; add buffer for downside risk, especially after recent spikes.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., 79.80 → 76.24), leading to overshoot in forecast; apply lagged smoothing or dampen initial slope after high peaks.
- Forecast mean tends to drift upward over 30-day horizon despite true price mean reversion; enforce short-term mean-reversion constraint (e.g., cap forecast at 1–2σ above recent 7-day average).
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; introduce sentiment-triggered correction: if sentiment drops below 0.33 after 10 days, reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- Avoid linear extrapolation after recent volatility; use sentiment + price momentum to weight forecast adjustments (e.g., if sentiment = 0.00 and price fell >5%, forecast should not rise >1σ above prior low).
